native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: Original papers in Experimental Economics are on average much longer (28.0 pages, N=18) than original papers in Psychology (11.2 pages, N=97) — roughly 2.5 times longer. This likely reflects journal format: the ee originals appeared in AER/QJE long-article format, while rpp originals come from Psychological Science / JEP:LMC, which include many 1–5 page short reports, making the rpp distribution right-skewed (median 9 vs mean 11.2) and cross-journal page comparisons approximate.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows x 57 cols). Verified ee and rpp have exactly one row per unique id (18 and 97 papers respectively; no double-counting); ml1/ml3 (592 and 220 rows, heavily lab-duplicated) excluded as separate projects. Confirmed 'length' is clean int64 with zero missing/non-numeric values. Computed mean/median/SD/range of length per group. The replication-success CSV (143 rows) was not used since it lacks a length column.
